When I was growing up, my older brother and I went to St. Thomas what felt like almost every summer. My mother’s side of the family is from St. Thomas. My mother, my aunts, and my uncle grew up there, and so did many of my cousins. My grandmother and grandfather were from St. Thomas as well, and my uncle still lives in the same house the family has had for years.

My mother still goes back to St. Thomas almost every year when she can, for Carnival and to visit my grandmother’s gravesite around Mother’s Day. 

Great video!

comments.author: @Lemmiwinks-u9p
comments.text: Lived there for year and a half. Video doesn’t talk about the racial animosity between native islanders and white “interlopers”. The island can’t sustain without professionals from the mainland coming to work such as medical professionals. The video mentions the “Frenchies” who are white Cajuns who also have been living in the islands for hundreds of years. They don’t take guff from the locals. They have their own system of justice. Stay on the beaten paths of Charlotte Amalie and no issues. Don’t leave valuables unattended on the beaches. The natural beauty of the islands especially St John are spectacular. Red Hook is the area to visit especially Duffy’s Love Shack.

comments.text: As AI videos go this is one of the better ones. That said you really didn't show what it's truly like to live there. It mentioned some of the challenges and glossed over the rest. The same government that wants the young people to stay are the ones engaged in the corruption that's making it impossible to have a decent standard of living. I lived there long enough to say I lived there and I'm thankful and grateful for all of my experiences there, that said I never want to live that close to the ground again. Most people and business have generators out of necessity and the people maintaining them are not paid a living wage. The maintenance crews keeping the massive properties full of air bombs don't fare much better. Owning a home there isn't out of reach because of prices there out of reach because getting a mortgage there isn't at all as easy as it is on the mainland. I wouldn't trade my time there for anything but I would love to see a video that shows the real St. Thomas.
